text:
To all my brothers and sisters

of the still-oppressed world.

Uniforms, machine guns,

courtyard, narrow corridors,

solid iron door,

black bolt and padlocks.

A mouth that opens

two yards by one and a half;

floors, ceilings, and walls

bare as the desert.

Tombs for the living

where specters crawl

whose only human thing

is the shape of the skeleton.

Even the walls seem

livelier and less dry!

Nowhere on earth are there

deeper pits

nor time that drags itself

along such motionless hands.

Nor can there be

a space so small

that hides so many pains,

that keeps so many secrets.

The corridors lie in wait

with hysterical lookout posts,

ambushes one can touch

like shackles of ice.

Five transistor radios

deafen the quiet air

so that the cries are not heard

in the night of torment.

Dark-backed racks

strike sparks from the wind,

but return beaten down,

their jaws hanging slack.

Either earth is very far away,

or heaven is very far away!

I do not know whether you know

what a prisoner then feels;

that climb of cold

from backbone to hair,

that trembling which slips

through the chinks of fear

and courage’s spur

blunted by powerless rage,

bound and helpless,

crucified in the stocks.

That ancient pain

that never had a cure,

of a cornered animal

struggling as a captive

at the mercy of those who use

cruelty as a right.

And to feel the soul filled with a hatred

that scrapes within!

They appear, like rats

from hell’s sewer,

before the man who has

no weapon but his silence.

translation.title: To All My Brothers and Sisters…
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The prison’s catalogued physical detail and the poem’s address to the oppressed are retained.
